eligibility: A primer for undergraduates moving into graduate geometric group theory, with example-driven instruction, exercises and research projects.
reason: The conversational office-hour format is explicitly a vehicle for specialist mathematical training.

eligibility: Cambridge's front matter identifies a graduate textbook and research reference on moonshine, finite groups, modular forms and vertex operator algebras, with nearly two hundred exercises.
reason: Connections to conformal field theory and string theory remain within a specialist technical training/reference purpose.

eligibility: The author's front matter expressly gives two purposes: a standard graduate algebraic-topology textbook and a reference for additional technical topics. Its four cores are fundamental groups, homology, cohomology and higher homotopy.
reason: Both stated purposes fall under H2, independently of the quality of its geometric explanations.

eligibility: A specialist development of the methods and proofs of prime distribution, with chapters on Dirichlet's theorem, Chebyshev's theorem, zeta functions and the prime number theorem and chapter exercises. The author explicitly distinguishes this technical purpose from a historical account of people and their motives.
reason: The chronological organization supports a specialist mathematical monograph; the decision follows the author's scope and method rather than the historical title.

eligibility: A chronological research survey organized by number-theory subtopics, with an extensive bibliographic apparatus, intended especially for graduate researchers and students locating earlier results.
reason: The publisher and contents establish specialist reference as its dominant function. Avoidance of detailed proofs broadens access but does not turn the research inventory into a general explanatory narrative.

author: Denis Choimet; Hervé Queffélec
eligibility: A technical exposition of advanced analysis theorems through complete and alternative proofs, worked examples and more than 150 exercises with solution hints, addressed to mathematical colleagues and graduate students.
reason: The historical introductions motivate an advanced mathematical study text. Corrected Choimet's given name from Didier to Denis using the publisher's foreword.

eligibility: A progressive introduction to performing differential and integral calculus, from constants and products through maxima, partial differentiation and area calculations.
reason: The verified publisher contents directly establish technical instruction as the main purpose.
reassessment: Reread the previous exclusion and independently checked the book's own publisher contents. Retain H2; no scores are assigned. The current evidence is specific to Thompson's book rather than an adjacent recommendation.

eligibility: AMS explicitly identifies graduate students and research mathematicians as the readership. The volume develops elliptic curves, p-adic numbers, zeta functions, number fields and Dedekind domains.
reason: The accessible overview remains a structured specialist introduction and supplementary technical study text.

eligibility: The second Iwanami number-theory volume develops local/global fields and class field theory, with Galois-theory support and answers to exercises.
reason: Its contents form specialist mathematical instruction, not a narrative history. AMS confirms the title and the Kato, Kurokawa and Saito authorship; the combined-series Google record is used only for contents.

eligibility: The third technical number-theory volume develops Iwasawa theory and modular forms, including zeta-regularized products, Kronecker's limit formula and the Selberg trace formula.
reason: The publisher's specified scope is specialist theoretical instruction/reference, notwithstanding motivation from Ramanujan's relations.

eligibility: Ghrist's text systematically teaches applied-topology tools from manifolds and Euler calculus through homology, Morse theory, sheaves and categories. The publisher description explicitly identifies self-study, course and supplementary-text uses.
reason: Every method is paired with an application, but the principal purpose remains acquiring specialist tools.

eligibility: The editors' preface explicitly defines the volume as a structured reference work for mathematicians, students and professionals who use mathematics, with cross-referenced technical articles.
reason: Broad applications and accessible motivation do not override its stated technical-reference purpose.

eligibility: Nielsen explicitly aims to teach mastery of neural-network concepts by writing code, building a network library and solving handwriting-recognition problems.
reason: A durable principle-based teaching approach still meets the technical skill-development exclusion. It is not classified from its software topic alone.

eligibility: A five-volume comprehensive differential-geometry text. Its first volume builds the technical language of manifolds, tensors, forms and metrics for the later geometry volumes.
reason: The full nomination is a systematic specialist learning/reference work. Historical perspectives in later volumes do not change the series' main structure.

eligibility: The publisher states that this chronological survey and extensive bibliography is aimed at number-theory researchers, to locate pre-1950 results, prevent rediscovery and find methods for current research.
reason: The explicit dominant function is specialist technical reference; the word Story in the title does not determine eligibility.
